title: A cloud plan pass reads 1104 tick records one at a time and outlives its own lease
description:
The cloud reconciler cannot plan a real repository. On 2026-09-20, run_b124d64a6399460cb53b3b8ce1dde41a spent OVER 14 MINUTES in plan-1 and had not finished:

    Status: Running
    publish-slot-1  ok    lease expires_at 19:14:06 (3 minute TTL)
    plan-1          running since 19:11, still running at 19:25

Mechanism: TrackerClient.#all() (tracker-client.ts:463) reads every tick record one at a time:

    const paths = await this.store.list(TICK_RECORD_DIR);
    for (const path of paths) {
      const file = await this.store.read(path);   // one GitHub round-trip, sequential
    }

pengelbrecht/ticks has 1104 records under .tick/issues. That is 1104 sequential HTTPS round-trips through the GitHub contents API per plan pass, and graph() calls #all() on EVERY pass (D33: every pass re-derives the world).

Two consequences, and the second is worse:

1. A plan pass takes ~10+ minutes where it should take one request.
2. The publish slot lease it holds has a 3-minute TTL and is not renewed during the read, so the lease EXPIRES mid-plan on every pass. The run holds a slot it no longer owns, and whatever depends on that lease being valid is running on a lie. The lease line disappears from `ticfac cloud status` while the run carries on.

This is invisible locally: the local reconciler reads .tick/ from a worktree on disk.

Fix shape - any of these alone would do, the first is the obvious one:
- Read the tracker in ONE request. GitHub's git/trees API with recursive=1 returns every path and blob sha for a ref; the contents of a whole directory can come from a single tree fetch plus blob reads, and the blobs can be fetched concurrently rather than in a loop.
- Failing that, bound the concurrency at something like 16 rather than 1.
- Renew the lease during a long read, or take the lease AFTER planning rather than before.

Also worth asking whether a plan needs all 1104 records at all: it needs the epic and its descendants. #all() exists to serve tk-shaped queries; graph() of one epic does not need the whole tracker.

Found by performing u9h - the first time an epic has been run on the deployed factory against a real repository.
acceptance_criteria: A plan pass against a repository with ~1100 tick records completes in seconds and holds a valid lease throughout, proven against the deployed factory
